spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m9p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT MaxEpoch
VARIABLES epoch, grantEpoch
Init == epoch = 1 /\ grantEpoch = 0
Request == grantEpoch = 0 /\ grantEpoch' = epoch /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Lift == grantEpoch = epoch /\ grantEpoch' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Reconfig == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ grantEpoch' = 0
Next == Request \/ Lift \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, grantEpoch>>
NoStaleGrant == grantEpoch = 0 \/ grantEpoch = epoch
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
MaxEpoch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleGrant
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is coordinated by a single yard controller that stamps every lift authorization with an epoch number. When the controller reconfigures the yard (for example after a crane goes offline), it advances to a new epoch and every previously issued grant becomes invalid. A crane may request a lift grant, which is stamped with the controller's current epoch; the crane may then perform one lift only while holding a grant whose epoch still matches the controller's current epoch. Grant requests, lifts, and reconfigurations can be observed by the cranes in any order, so a grant issued under an old epoch might still be sitting in a crane's inbox after a reconfiguration. The safety concern is that a crane must never perform a lift using a grant left over from a superseded epoch. We model the current epoch, the epoch stamped on the outstanding grant (zero when none is held), and a bounded count of completed lifts.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A crane never holds an outstanding lift grant whose stamped epoch differs from the controller's current epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m0p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT MaxVer
Patrons == {1, 2}
VARIABLES held, ver, snap
Init == held = [p \in Patrons |-> FALSE] /\ ver = 0 /\ snap = [p \in Patrons |-> 99]
Read(p) == snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = ver] /\ UNCHANGED <<held, ver>>
Reserve(p) == snap[p] = ver /\ ver < MaxVer /\ (\A q \in Patrons : ~held[q])
              /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
              /\ ver' = ver + 1
              /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = 99]
Release(p) == held[p] /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap>>
Next == \E p \in Patrons : Read(p) \/ Reserve(p) \/ Release(p)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<held, ver, snap>>
MutualExclusion == \A p, q \in Patrons : (p # q) => ~(held[p] /\ held[q])
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A library book reservation system lets two patrons compete for the same rare book using optimistic concurrency control. The book record carries a version number. To reserve, a patron first reads the current version into a private snapshot, then later attempts to commit the reservation; the commit succeeds only if the version has not changed since the read (the optimistic check) and no other patron currently holds the book. A successful commit marks the patron as holder and bumps the version, so any competitor working from a stale snapshot must re-read and retry. A patron may be slow, sitting on an old snapshot for a long time, but is never considered failed. The safety requirement is that the book is a critical resource that at most one patron may hold at any instant. We model, for each patron, whether they hold the book and their last-read version snapshot, plus the book's shared version number.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct patrons hold the book at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES spool, lease
Init == spool = [load |-> 0, cap |-> 2] /\ lease = 0
Submit == spool.load < spool.cap /\ spool' = [spool EXCEPT !.load = @ + 1] /\ UNCHANGED lease
Acquire == lease = 0 /\ lease' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED spool
Drain == lease > 0 /\ spool.load > 0 /\ spool' = [spool EXCEPT !.load = @ - 1] /\ lease' = lease - 1
Tick == lease > 0 /\ lease' = lease - 1 /\ UNCHANGED spool
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= spool.load /\ spool' = [spool EXCEPT !.cap = c] /\ UNCHANGED lease
Next == Submit \/ Acquire \/ Drain \/ Tick \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<spool, lease>>
WithinCapacity == spool.load >= 0 /\ spool.load <= spool.cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler that buffers submitted print jobs before they reach the presses. The spooler has a capacity that an operator can change at runtime, raising it when a fast press comes online or lowering it when a press is taken out for maintenance. A press must hold a short-lived lease before it may pull jobs from the spool; the lease counts down over time and expires, after which another press may acquire it. New jobs may be submitted only while the spool has room, and the operator may lower capacity but never below the number of jobs currently buffered. The safety requirement is that the number of buffered jobs never exceeds the spooler's current capacity. We model the spool as a record holding its current load and capacity, together with the remaining time on the outstanding press lease.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of buffered jobs never exceeds the spooler's current capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m9p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES epoch, capacity, load
Init == epoch = 1 /\ capacity = 3 /\ load = 0
Assign == load < capacity /\ load' = load + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>
Complete == load > 0 /\ load' = load - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>
Reconfig == epoch < 3 /\ \E c \in {2, 3, 4} : c >= load /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ capacity' = c /\ UNCHANGED load
Next == Assign \/ Complete \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, capacity, load>>
CapacityRespected == load >= 0 /\ load <= capacity
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is run by a dispatcher that tracks how many passenger requests are currently in service across all cars. When a car is added to or removed from service the dispatcher performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration: it advances to a new epoch and sets a new service capacity reflecting the cars now available. Passenger requests may be assigned only while the number in service is below the current capacity, and each completed trip frees a slot. When lowering capacity during a reconfiguration the dispatcher never sets it below the number of trips already in service. The safety requirement is that the number of in-service trips never exceeds the current capacity even as capacity changes at runtime. We model the dispatcher's current epoch, its current capacity, and the count of trips in service.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of in-service trips never exceeds the current capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m7p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Hubs == {1, 2}
VARIABLES reg, ver, snap
Init == reg = 0 /\ ver = 0 /\ snap = [h \in Hubs |-> 99]
Read(h) == snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![h] = ver] /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver>>
Commit(h) == snap[h] = ver /\ ver < 3
             /\ reg' = reg + 1
             /\ ver' = ver + 1
             /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![h] = 99]
Next == \E h \in Hubs : Read(h) \/ Commit(h)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, ver, snap>>
NoLostUpdate == reg = ver
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps a shared lock-state register that two independent hub instances may update. The register carries a value and a version number. Each hub updates the register with a compare-and-swap: it first reads the current version into a private snapshot, and its write commits only if the version is still what it read, in which case both the value and the version advance by one. If another hub committed in between, the snapshot is stale and the write must be retried against the fresh version, so no update silently overwrites another. Two independent hubs share this one register pool and race to update it. The safety requirement is that no update is ever lost: because every committed change advances value and version together in lockstep, the register value always equals its version. We model the register value, its version, and each hub's last-read snapshot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The register value always equals its version, so no committed update is ever lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Techs == {1, 2}
VARIABLES coarse, fine, override
Init == coarse = 0 /\ fine = 0 /\ override = FALSE
AcquireCoarse(t) == coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = t /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, override>>
AcquireFine(t) == coarse = t /\ fine = 0 /\ fine' = t /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, override>>
ReleaseFine(t) == fine = t /\ fine' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, override>>
ReleaseCoarse(t) == coarse = t /\ fine = 0 /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, override>>
TurnOn == ~override /\ override' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>
TurnOff == override /\ (fine = 0 \/ fine = coarse) /\ override' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>
AdminFine(t) == override /\ fine = 0 /\ fine' = t /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, override>>
Next == \E t \in Techs : AcquireCoarse(t) \/ AcquireFine(t) \/ ReleaseFine(t) \/ ReleaseCoarse(t) \/ AdminFine(t)
        \/ TurnOn \/ TurnOff
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, override>>
LockHierarchy == fine = 0 \/ fine = coarse \/ override
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LockHierarchy
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker protects its cold storage with hierarchical locks: a technician must first take the coarse lock on a refrigerator before taking the fine lock on an individual shelf inside it, and only the holder of both may adjust that shelf's inventory. This two-level discipline stops a stale or unauthorized technician from touching a shelf they have not properly locked from the top down. The system also supports a privileged admin override: while the override is active an administrator may act on a shelf directly, bypassing the coarse-before-fine rule for emergencies. Technicians acquire and release locks in order, and the override can be toggled on or off. The safety requirement is that, absent the admin override, a shelf's fine lock is only ever held by the technician who also holds the enclosing refrigerator's coarse lock. We model which technician holds the coarse lock, which holds the fine lock, and whether the admin override is active.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Unless the admin override is active, the fine lock is only ever held by the technician who holds the coarse lock.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m3p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Nodes == {1, 2}
VARIABLES leader, alive, driving
Init == leader = 0 /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE] /\ driving = {}
Elect(n) == alive[n] /\ leader = 0 /\ leader' = n /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, driving>>
Crash(n) == alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, driving>>
Recover(n) == ~alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, driving>>
StepDown == leader # 0 /\ ~alive[leader] /\ leader' = 0 /\ driving' = {} /\ UNCHANGED alive
StartDrive(n) == leader = n /\ alive[n] /\ driving = {} /\ driving' = {n} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>
StopDrive(n) == n \in driving /\ driving' = driving \ {n} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>
Next == \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Recover(n) \/ StartDrive(n) \/ StopDrive(n) \/ StepDown
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, alive, driving>>
ExclusiveDrive == \A a, b \in Nodes : (a \in driving /\ b \in driving) => a = b
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveDrive
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line is driven by a set of station controllers that elect a single leader to advance the conveyor, which is the one critical resource of the line. If the current leader crashes silently, a failover elects a new leader from the controllers that are still alive, and the dead leader's hold on the conveyor is released. Only the current leader, while alive, may engage the conveyor drive, and a controller must stop driving before another may take over. One controller can crash without warning at any moment, and a crashed controller may later recover and rejoin. The safety requirement is that the conveyor drive is a critical resource under mutual exclusion: at no instant may two different controllers both be driving it. We model which controller is leader, which controllers are alive, and the set of controllers currently driving the conveyor.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At no instant do two different controllers both drive the conveyor.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m9p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Feeders == {1, 2}
VARIABLES epoch, cap, draw
Total == draw[1] + draw[2]
Init == epoch = 1 /\ cap = 3 /\ draw = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
Increase(f) == draw[f] < 2 /\ Total < cap /\ draw' = [draw EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1] /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>
Decrease(f) == draw[f] > 0 /\ draw' = [draw EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1] /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap>>
Reconfig == epoch < 3 /\ \E c \in {2, 3, 4} : c >= Total /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED draw
Next == (\E f \in Feeders : Increase(f) \/ Decrease(f)) \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, cap, draw>>
LoadWithinCapacity == draw[1] + draw[2] <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadWithinCapacity
nl:
A power-grid load shedder balances draw across two feeders against a total capacity budget. When grid conditions change the controller performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration, advancing to a new epoch and setting a new capacity budget for the combined draw. A feeder may increase its draw only while the combined draw across both feeders stays within the current capacity, and it may shed load to decrease its draw at any time. During a reconfiguration the controller never sets the new capacity below the combined draw already committed. The safety requirement is that the combined draw across the feeders never exceeds the current capacity budget, even as that budget changes at runtime. We model the current epoch, the current capacity budget, and the per-feeder draw as a function.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The combined draw across both feeders never exceeds the current capacity budget.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m4p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Slots == {1, 2}
VARIABLES queue, alloc
Init == queue = 0 /\ alloc = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
Admit == queue < 2 /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED alloc
Allocate(s) == queue > 0 /\ alloc[s] = 0 /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = 1] /\ queue' = queue - 1
Free(s) == alloc[s] = 1 /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = 0] /\ UNCHANGED queue
Next == Admit \/ (\E s \in Slots : Allocate(s) \/ Free(s))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, alloc>>
NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : alloc[s] <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction feeds incoming orders through a bounded work queue with backpressure before assigning each to a fixed matching slot. Two independent matching instances share one pool of slots and race to place queued orders. New orders are admitted to the queue only while it has room, which is the backpressure that prevents overload. To place an order, an instance picks a slot that is currently empty and marks it filled, dequeuing one order; a slot may later be freed when its match settles. The safety requirement is that the same slot is never allocated twice: no instance may place an order into a slot that is already filled. We model the count of queued orders and the fill state of each slot as a function.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever allocated to more than one order at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m7p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Hubs == {1, 2}
VARIABLES active, ver, cap, snap
Init == active = 0 /\ ver = 0 /\ cap = 2 /\ snap = [h \in Hubs |-> 99]
Read(h) == snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![h] = ver] /\ UNCHANGED <<active, ver, cap>>
Acquire(h) == snap[h] = ver /\ ver < 3 /\ active < cap
              /\ active' = active + 1 /\ ver' = ver + 1
              /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![h] = 99] /\ UNCHANGED cap
Release == active > 0 /\ active' = active - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, cap, snap>>
AdminRaise == cap' = 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<active, ver, snap>>
AdminLower == active <= 2 /\ cap' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<active, ver, snap>>
Next == (\E h \in Hubs : Read(h) \/ Acquire(h)) \/ Release \/ AdminRaise \/ AdminLower
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<active, ver, cap, snap>>
SessionsWithinCapacity == active >= 0 /\ active <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SessionsWithinCapacity
nl:
A smart-home door lock network tracks how many unlock sessions are simultaneously active using a shared compare-and-swap register. Two hubs coordinate through this register, each reading the current version into a snapshot and committing an increment only if the version still matches, so concurrent grants do not clobber the active-session count. The number of active sessions may not exceed the current session capacity. A privileged admin override may raise the capacity to allow extra sessions during a service window, and may later lower it again, but only when the number of active sessions already fits under the reduced capacity. Sessions end and decrement the active count. The safety requirement is that the number of active unlock sessions never exceeds the current capacity. We model the active-session count, the register version, the current capacity, and each hub's read snapshot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of active unlock sessions never exceeds the current capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m3p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Insts == {1, 2}
Total == 3
VARIABLES stock, dispensed, leader, alive
Init == stock = Total /\ dispensed = 0 /\ leader = 0 /\ alive = [n \in Insts |-> TRUE]
Elect(n) == alive[n] /\ leader = 0 /\ leader' = n /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, alive>>
Crash(n) == alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, leader>>
Recover(n) == ~alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, leader>>
StepDown == leader # 0 /\ ~alive[leader] /\ leader' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dispensed, alive>>
Dispense(n) == leader = n /\ alive[n] /\ stock > 0
               /\ stock' = stock - 1 /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>
Next == (\E n \in Insts : Elect(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Recover(n) \/ Dispense(n)) \/ StepDown
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<stock, dispensed, leader, alive>>
PillsConserved == stock + dispensed = Total
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PillsConserved
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser draws pills from a single shared stock pool served by two independent dispenser instances. The instances elect a single leader that is permitted to dispense; if the leader crashes silently, a failover steps it down and a surviving instance is elected in its place. Only the current alive leader may dispense, removing one pill from stock and adding it to the running dispensed tally. Because every dispensed pill is exactly one pill removed from stock, nothing is created or destroyed. The safety requirement is conservation: the pills remaining in stock plus the pills already dispensed always equal the original stock total. We model the remaining stock, the dispensed tally, which instance is leader, and which instances are alive.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The remaining stock plus the dispensed tally always equals the original stock total.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Fleet == 3
VARIABLES waiting, running, cap
Init == waiting = Fleet /\ running = 0 /\ cap = 2
Enter == waiting > 0 /\ running < cap /\ waiting' = waiting - 1 /\ running' = running + 1 /\ UNCHANGED cap
Exit == running > 0 /\ running' = running - 1 /\ waiting' = waiting + 1 /\ UNCHANGED cap
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= running /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, running>>
Next == Enter \/ Exit \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<waiting, running, cap>>
FleetConserved == waiting + running = Fleet
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FleetConserved
nl:
A subway signalling block system regulates a fixed fleet of trains that circulate between a holding area and the running blocks. Entry requests pass through a bounded work queue whose backpressure prevents a train from entering the running section once the number of trains on the line has reached the current capacity. A waiting train enters a running block only while occupancy is below capacity; a train that finishes its run exits and returns to the holding area. The line's capacity can change at runtime as blocks are opened or closed, but the controller never lowers capacity below the number of trains already running. Because trains only move between holding and running and none are added or removed, the fleet is conserved. The safety requirement is that the number of waiting trains plus the number of running trains always equals the fixed fleet size. We model the count of waiting trains, the count of running trains, and the current capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of waiting trains plus the number of running trains always equals the fixed fleet size.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m4p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES queue, paid, dispenses, override
Init == queue = 0 /\ paid = FALSE /\ dispenses = 0 /\ override = FALSE
Admit == queue < 2 /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<paid, dispenses, override>>
Pay == queue > 0 /\ ~paid /\ dispenses = 0 /\ paid' = TRUE /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<dispenses, override>>
Dispense == paid /\ dispenses = 0 /\ dispenses' = 1 /\ paid' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, override>>
ToggleOverride == override' = ~override /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, paid, dispenses>>
AdminReset == override /\ dispenses' = 0 /\ paid' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, override>>
Next == Admit \/ Pay \/ Dispense \/ ToggleOverride \/ AdminReset
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, paid, dispenses, override>>
DispenseAtMostOnce == dispenses <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A vending machine network processes payments through a bounded work queue with backpressure before releasing an item. Payment requests are admitted to the queue only while it has room. Taking a payment marks the current item as paid and ready. Releasing the item is an irreversible action: once the paid item is dispensed it cannot be dispensed again in the same cycle. A privileged admin override may reset the machine to begin a fresh cycle, clearing the paid state and the dispense record. The safety requirement is that within a single cycle the irreversible dispense action happens at most once. We model the count of queued payments, whether the current item is paid and ready, how many times the current item has been dispensed, and whether the admin override is engaged.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Within a single cycle the item is dispensed at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Boxes == {1, 2}
VARIABLES phase, vote, commits, cap
Init == phase = 0 /\ vote = [b \in Boxes |-> 0] /\ commits = 0 /\ cap = 2
StartVoting == phase = 0 /\ phase' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, commits, cap>>
Cast(b) == phase = 1 /\ vote[b] = 0 /\ \E v \in {1, 2} : vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![b] = v]
           /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, commits, cap>>
Commit == phase = 1 /\ (\A b \in Boxes : vote[b] = 1) /\ commits = 0
          /\ commits' = 1 /\ phase' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, cap>>
Abort == phase = 1 /\ (\E b \in Boxes : vote[b] = 2) /\ phase' = 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, commits, cap>>
Reset == phase \in {2, 3} /\ phase' = 0 /\ vote' = [b \in Boxes |-> 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<commits, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, commits>>
Next == StartVoting \/ (\E b \in Boxes : Cast(b)) \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Reset \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, vote, commits, cap>>
CommitAtMostOnce == commits <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommitAtMostOnce
nl:
A subway signalling block system uses two-phase commit across two signal boxes to decide whether a train may take a contested junction. A coordinator opens a voting round, each signal box votes yes or no, and the junction is committed to the train only if both boxes vote yes; any no vote aborts the round. Committing the junction is an irreversible action that must happen at most once across the whole run, so once the junction has been granted it is never granted a second time even if later rounds are opened. The block capacity can be reconfigured at runtime as the coordinator adjusts its buffer. The safety requirement is that the irreversible commit of the junction happens at most once. We model the round phase, each signal box's vote, the number of commits made, and the reconfigurable capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The junction is committed at most once across the entire run.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m3p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Nodes == {1, 2}
Reqs == {1, 2}
VARIABLES leader, alive, finalized, pending
Init == leader = 0 /\ alive = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE] /\ finalized = 0 /\ pending = {}
Submit(s) == pending' = pending \cup {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, finalized>>
Elect(n) == alive[n] /\ leader = 0 /\ leader' = n /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, finalized, pending>>
Crash(n) == alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, finalized, pending>>
Recover(n) == ~alive[n] /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, finalized, pending>>
StepDown == leader # 0 /\ ~alive[leader] /\ leader' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, finalized, pending>>
Finalize(s) == leader # 0 /\ alive[leader] /\ s \in pending /\ finalized = 0
               /\ finalized' = 1 /\ pending' = pending \ {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>
Next == (\E s \in Reqs : Submit(s) \/ Finalize(s)) \/ (\E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Recover(n)) \/ StepDown
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, alive, finalized, pending>>
FinalizeAtMostOnce == finalized <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FinalizeAtMostOnce
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler runs on two redundant nodes that elect a single leader to finalize bookings. Surgery requests arrive and sit in a pending pool that may be served in any order, since request messages can be reordered in transit. Only the current alive leader may finalize a booking, which is an irreversible action: once a surgery slot has been finalized it is committed and must never be finalized a second time. If the leader crashes silently, a failover steps it down and a surviving node is elected. The safety requirement is that the irreversible finalize action happens at most once. We model which node is leader, which nodes are alive, the count of finalizations performed, and the pool of pending requests.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A booking is finalized at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Boxes == {1, 2}
VARIABLES phase, vote, occ, cap
Init == phase = 0 /\ vote = [b \in Boxes |-> 0] /\ occ = 0 /\ cap = 2
StartVoting == phase = 0 /\ phase' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, occ, cap>>
Cast(b) == phase = 1 /\ vote[b] = 0 /\ \E v \in {1, 2} : vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![b] = v]
           /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, occ, cap>>
Commit == phase = 1 /\ (\A b \in Boxes : vote[b] = 1) /\ occ < cap
          /\ occ' = occ + 1 /\ phase' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, cap>>
Abort == phase = 1 /\ (\E b \in Boxes : vote[b] = 2) /\ phase' = 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, occ, cap>>
Reset == phase \in {2, 3} /\ phase' = 0 /\ vote' = [b \in Boxes |-> 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, cap>>
Depart == occ > 0 /\ occ' = occ - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, cap>>

The capacity can be reconfigured at runtime, but the controller never lowers it below current occupancy. The safety requirement is that occupancy of the running section never exceeds the current capacity. We model the round phase, each box's vote, the current occupancy, and the reconfigurable capacity.

AcqFine(t) == locks.coarse = t /\ locks.fine = 0 /\ locks' = [locks EXCEPT !.fine = t] /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ver, cap>>
Update(t) == locks.coarse = t /\ locks.fine = t /\ ver < cap
             /\ rec' = rec + 1 /\ ver' = ver + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<locks, cap>>
RelFine(t) == locks.fine = t /\ locks' = [locks EXCEPT !.fine = 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ver, cap>>
RelCoarse(t) == locks.coarse = t /\ locks.fine = 0 /\ locks' = [locks EXCEPT !.coarse = 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, ver, cap>>

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet updates a shared inventory record under hierarchical locks: a robot must first take the coarse zone lock, then the fine bin lock, and only while holding both may it apply an update. This top-down locking serializes updates so that none is lost. Each applied update advances both the record value and an update version by one, so a lost update, an overwrite not reflected in the version, would show up as the record and version drifting apart. The number of updates the buffer can absorb is a capacity that changes at runtime, and it is never lowered below the number of updates already applied. The safety requirement is that no update is ever lost: the record value always equals the update version. We model the lock state as a record of the coarse and fine holders, the record value, the update version, and the reconfigurable capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The record value always equals the update version, so no update is lost.

spec_text:

EXTENDS Naturals

Admit == queue < cap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, onArm>>
Load(b) == queue > 0 /\ onArm = {} /\ onArm' = {b} /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED cap
Unload(b) == b \in onArm /\ onArm' = onArm \ {b} /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= queue /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, onArm>>

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveArm
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags through a bounded work queue with backpressure toward a single sorter arm. Bags are admitted to the queue only while it has room, which is the backpressure that keeps the router from overloading. The sorter arm is the one critical resource: at most one bag may be on the arm at any instant. A queued bag is loaded onto the arm only when the arm is clear, and it is unloaded when routing completes. The queue's capacity changes at runtime as lanes open and close, but is never dropped below the number of bags already queued. The safety requirement is mutual exclusion of the sorter arm: two different bags are never on the arm at the same time. We model the number of queued bags, the reconfigurable queue capacity, and the set of bags currently on the arm.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Two different bags are never on the sorter arm at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m5p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
Slots == {1, 2}
VARIABLES alloc, votes, target

Propose(s) == target = 0 /\ alloc[s] = 0 /\ target' = s /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED alloc
CastVote == target # 0 /\ votes < 2 /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, target>>
Commit == target # 0 /\ votes >= 2 /\ alloc[target] = 0
          /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![target] = 1] /\ target' = 0 /\ votes' = 0
Free(s) == alloc[s] = 1 /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![s] = 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, target>>
Next == (\E s \in Slots : Propose(s) \/ Free(s)) \/ CastVote \/ Commit

NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : alloc[s] <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker requires quorum voting before any storage slot is allocated. Two independent instances share one pool of slots and may each open a proposal to allocate a specific free slot. Voters cast approvals for the open proposal, and the allocation commits only once a quorum of approvals is reached, at which point the target slot is marked filled. A slot may later be freed. Because a proposal only ever targets a currently free slot and commits at most one fill to it, the same slot is never allocated twice. The safety requirement is that no slot is ever allocated to more than one claim at a time. We model the fill state of each slot as a function, the vote count for the open proposal, and which slot the open proposal targets.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever allocated to more than one claim at the same time.

spec_text:

EXTENDS Naturals

Acquire(i) == holder = 0 /\ holder' = i /\ timer' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED using
Use(i) == holder = i /\ timer > 0 /\ using = {} /\ using' = {i} /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, timer>>
Done(i) == i \in using /\ using' = using \ {i} /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, timer>>
Tick == timer > 0 /\ timer' = timer - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, using>>
Expire == holder # 0 /\ timer = 0 /\ using = {} /\ holder' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<timer, using>>
Next == (\E i \in Insts : Acquire(i) \/ Use(i) \/ Done(i)) \/ Tick \/ Expire

====

NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveHopper
nl:
A vending machine network shares one coin hopper between two independent machine instances, each of which must hold a short-lived lease before touching the hopper. A machine acquires the lease only while it is free, and the lease counts down and expires, after which another machine may take it. Only a machine holding a live lease may actually use the hopper, and the hopper is the critical resource: at most one machine may be using it at any instant. A machine finishes and releases the hopper, and a lease may only expire once the hopper is no longer in use. The safety requirement is mutual exclusion of the hopper: two different machines are never using it at the same time. We model which machine holds the lease, the time remaining on the lease, and the set of machines currently using the hopper.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Two different machines are never using the coin hopper at the same time.

Renew == leased > 0 /\ timer' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<free, leased>>

A controller leases a block token from the free pool, moving it into the leased set and starting a lease timer; the lease counts down and expires, returning the token to the free pool. A live lease may be renewed to reset its timer. Because tokens only ever move between the free pool and the leased set and none are minted or destroyed, the total number of tokens is conserved. The safety requirement is conservation: the number of free tokens plus the number of leased tokens always equals the fixed pool size.
